old: As you listen, a sensation, image, phrase, feeling, objection, or silence may become noticeable. Let the next invitation follow that response. Use warmth, a boundary, direction, or more time as needed. Finish with the complete return, then note what happened and any real-world action it calls for.
new: As you listen, when you notice that something is happening for you (a sensation, an image, a phrase, a feeling, an objection or even a recognition of silence), then respond to the next invitation (using as much or as little warmth, boundary, direction and time as is needed), until you have come completely back, and then notice what has happened for you (including any actions that need to be taken in the “real” world).

old: When you become panicky, disoriented, increasingly unreal, or less able to function, stop deepening and return to the room and appropriate support. A difficult feeling you freely choose to stay with while present is a different situation.
new: Note: If at any time you feel panicky, or out of it, or more unreal, or incapable of functioning appropriately, then do not go any further, but simply come back to the room and access the appropriate support for yourself. This is quite different from choosing to deal freely with a difficult feeling, and remaining in touch with yourself as you do so.

old: “What exactly is being claimed?” “What choice is being framed as inevitable?” “What is being presupposed?” “Who benefits if I accept this frame?” “What emotion is being amplified?” “What information is missing?” “Can I say no without being punished, shamed, mocked, abandoned, or spiritually downgraded?”
new: WHAT are they trying to sell me? WHAT are they trying to make seem inevitable? WHAT are they assuming? WHO benefits from the frame? WHAT emotions are being pumped up? WHAT information is being kept from me? COULD I say ‘NO’ without being punished/shamed/mocked/abandoned/spiritually demoted?

old: A useful guide leaves the adult self more present. Powerful states need stronger boundaries.
new: The more powerful the state, the more guideposts that it might be useful for the adult part of yourself to have at hand.

old: Permissive words can still conceal coercion. I watch for the following:
new: In spite of the use of permissive words, coercion may appear in the form of:

old: Indirect suggestion can slip past the skeptical guard because the conscious mind may never receive one clean proposition to accept or reject. The intended direction can still be quite specific even when the wording feels open, vague, conversational, or merely suggestive.
new: suggestions which, though indirect, and therefore able to circumvent the critical factor, may be very specific in where they are trying to lead the subject. This is done by using vague, conversational, or suggestive words

old: Induction hidden inside explanation: attention is being narrowed while the speaker pretends only to inform. Even an “anti-hypnosis” lesson can use induction mechanics.
new: inductive procedures embedded in what appears to be explanatory material. Remember that the act of explaining something, even about how not to be hypnotized, narrows the attention of the subject and is therefore making use of the mechanics of induction

old: Every answer means compliance: “yes,” “no,” noticing, not noticing, resistance, and silence are all redefined as proof that the suggestion is working.
new: causing the subject to give answers, whether they are “yes” or “no” or whether they notice something or not, that mean that they are being compliant. Resistance or even lack of response may also be redefined as being compliant

old: “Whether you notice it or not” binds: uncertainty is converted into invisible success that cannot be checked.
new: utilizing the “whether or not you notice it” bind

old: Identity and ownership language: safety or goodness becomes tied to obedience, a role, the guide’s approval, or belonging to someone else.
new: statements that equate a sense of self, or a sense that something is safe or good with the subject obeying, taking on a certain role, looking to the guide for approval, or being part of someone else.

old: Unannounced fractionation: moving in and out of absorption without telling you that repeated re-entry is part of the method.
new: They do fractionation (dipping in and out of an absorbed state) without telling you that you’re going to be brought back in again.

old: Hidden post-session cues: words, gestures, blinks, sounds, or repeated listening are meant to produce later behavior that was not plainly disclosed.
new: They give you cues (words, gestures, blinks, sounds, etc.) or make you listen to something repeatedly to influence later behavior, without telling you about it.

old: Amnesia or truth inflation: dreamlike material, missing memory, imagery, or body sensations are treated as proof of what happened.
new: They convince you that you’re in a dream-like state, have amnesia, or are in a state where images or body sensations are real.

old: An exit that does not exit: the recording ends while preserving a role, reduced judgment, impaired movement, blankness, or an indefinite altered state.
new: They don’t let you out cleanly, or they leave you in a role, with reduced ability to judge or move, in a blank state, or in some other altered state for an indefinite period of time at the end of the recording.

old: A real choice includes at least one branch that doesn’t continue the induction: make it lighter, change the method, remain fully alert, pause, or stop. No remains no. Silence and uncertainty don’t become consent because the narrator has a soothing voice.
new: There is at least one way to opt out (try something else, do something easier, stay completely alert, take a break, or stop), and “no” really means “no” (them saying “yes” doesn’t mean “no”, not knowing whether you want to or not is okay, and just because their voices sounds soothing doesn’t mean you have to do anything).

old: Appendix C has the longer de-hypnosis checklist.
new: (See Appendix C for the longer checklist for de-hypnosis.)

old: “Wise subconscious, please help me look at this impulse clearly. If part of this signal belongs to family programming, religious fear, marketing, erotic imprinting, political tribe, trauma response, or a childhood bargain for belonging, let that part become visible as conditioning. Let it soften or step back only as much as is safe. Leave behind whatever belongs to true guidance, the universal heart, and a better ordinary life. Let my body feel the difference.”
For daydreaming:
“If this daydream is useful, reveal the guidance inside it. If it is avoidance, bring me gently into the present and help me deal with what I need to deal with.”
For anxiety:
“What is anxiety trying to protect, and what would help it trust the adult self?”
For hidden truth:
“If the full truth would overwhelm me, please do not reveal it all. Show me the capacity before the content.”
For integration:
“What ordinary-life action would prove that I heard correctly?”
The prompt defines the search. NLP language affects how gently the question enters. Used together, they can create a safer field for an answer without pretending the answer is automatically true.
new: Experiment with the prompt. For instance if it's possible that the thought or feeling that brought the signal may be conditioned, such as from family, religion, marketing, erotic imprinting, politics, trauma, or childhood coping, state to be revealed and perhaps disarmed only the conditioned parts, leaving intact guidance from true sources, universal heart, and simply want to live a better life. An example may be, "My wise subconscious, if this signal is conditioned in any way from any source, please reveal that to me and disarm only the conditioned parts, leaving intact any guidance from the universal heart or from my real desire to have a better life.

If the signal involves daydreaming, perhaps state, "If this is useful to me in some way, please reveal that to me, but if it is simply a way of avoiding dealing with life in the present, please bring me back to the present and help me to deal with what needs to be dealt with in the present."
If the signal is anxiety, perhaps say,
If there is the possibility that the truth may be too much for the querent, state that,
And finally, to integrate, ask what needs to be done in normal life to demonstrate the answer was received
Remember, the prompt and NLP are two parts that can be used together to increase the safety of getting an answer. However, that does not mean that the answer is automatically safe.
